To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the generalized Bogomlo’nyi bound, which is the main result of the first paper, is invariant under the duality group of String Theory, and that supersymmetry is consistent with T duality only when primary scalar hair is present.

the observable charges of four dimensional point-like objects whose asymptotic behaviour constitutes a subclass closed by duality transform into two complex four dimensional representations of the full duality group and that the generalized Bogomoli’ni bound is an U ( 2, 2 ) -invariant built out with one representation while the other (which includes angular momentum) never appears in it.

all known four dimensional supersymmetric black holes are T dual in the time direction, that primary scalar hair must be included in the generalized BPS bound, that the bound is manifestly U(2, 2) invariant, and that the other representation of the U(2, 2) duality group never appears in the bound.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the transformation properties under the full String theory duality group of all the charges associated with the asymptotic behavior of four dimensional point-like objects.
the transformation of the charges and the Bogomol’niy bound of black holes under duality and with the consistency between supersymmetry and duality.
the transformation properties of the observable charges of four-dimensional pointlike objects, which are the asymptotic behavior of the corresponding space-times.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
supersymmetry, T duality, and S duality together require that primary scalar charges are included in the generalized bound.
all the known supersymmetric black holes are the time T duals of other black holes and the only black holes with no primary scalar hair are the supersymmetric ones.
the duality group acts on all observable charges of four-dimensional pointlike objects in the same way as it acts on the mass, electric charge and angular momentum of four dimensional black holes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the full duality group is not a symmetry of the black holes but a symmetry of the space of black holes.
the duality-invariant generalized Bogomolnyi bound is a powerful tool for the study of black holes.
all four dimensional pointlike solutions of String Theory with the asymptotic behavior studied here can be obtained from each other by a sequence of T and S duality transformations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
duality transformations are a powerful tool to find solutions of supergravity.
the generalized Bogomoli’nyi bound and the transformation of the observable charges under the full duality group of String Theory can be derived from the supersymmetry algebra.
the duality group is a symmetry of the theory and it is not just a remnant of the fact that we are using a particular string theory compactified on a particular manifold.
